verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents its own tap-trust control: tapping a third-party repository does not grant whole-tap trust, and users trust only the fully qualified items they install. That is a first-party supply-chain protection against untrusted package sources, and the community welcomed it. However, the evidence shows nothing like blocking install scripts or a minimum release age, and a user explicitly asks for a cooldown because new versions land within hours. Missing for 10: minimum release age or cooldown enforcement, blocking or sandboxing package build/install scripts, an admin-enforceable policy switch, and depth of documentation for tap trust.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can turn on protections against malicious packages, such as blocking lifecycle scripts or enforcing a minimum release age

citations.quote: Tapping a repository does not grant whole-tap trust. Install a fully qualified item to trust only that item
"Hell yeah, tap trust!!!" — positive reaction to new brew tap trust feature described in docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust.
